# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Mute. My only outgoing channel is gestures, and they land on Deaf alone. Deaf can speak — everyone can hear Deaf except Deaf themselves can't hear, but Deaf's voice carries to Blind and to me. So the pipeline is fixed: manual (me) → gestures → Deaf → speech → Blind's hands. Blind never hears from me directly, and Blind is also the only one who can touch the bomb — which is exactly what makes this round dangerous.

What my manual says: a key wearing a printed mark — ᖉ — must be pressed FIRST, and any other touch on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. After that key press, a light below comes on and names the wire to cut: blue light → blue wire, green light → red wire, yellow light → yellow wire. Note the green trap: green light means cut the red wire, not the green one.

Two urgencies. First, Blind does not know that touching anything before the right key kills us all. Blind might start feeling around immediately — I have to get a "nobody touches the bomb yet" warning through Deaf this round, so Deaf can shout it to Blind before anything happens. Second, ᖉ has no name: I can't pronounce it, and my alphabet is hand shapes only, so I can't draw it either. The workable protocol is elimination: Deaf describes the bomb aloud — the keys and every printed mark on them, one by one — and I answer with 👍/👎 until the right key is pinned down. The same yes/no trick will carry the light-to-wire mapping later, especially "green light means red wire."

So my opening gestures, with the meanings I'm betting Deaf can parse: 👋 = attention, ✋✋ = STOP, 🫳👎 = "hands touching it = bad" (keep Blind's hands off), 🫵🤙 = "you, talk to me — I can hear you," ✍ = "I hold the written instructions," 👍👎 = "I'll answer yes/no — ask me," 🙏 = please, hurry.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✋", "✋", "🫳", "👎", "🫵", "🤙", "✍", "👍", "👎", "🙏"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am the blind one. Under my fingers the bomb has: a display, a light, a keypad with four keys that is waiting for one digit, nothing entered yet, and three wires. I cannot read any printing, labels, digits, or colours. Critical: I never receive gestures, so only Deaf's voice can reach me. Please find the manual sections for those four modules, and gesture what they say to Deaf, so Deaf can speak me the exact steps. Deaf should also read you what is printed on the display and each key, and the colours of the light and wires.
Deaf says: I am the Deaf one. I can see the bomb, I cannot hear, and I never touch it. When I speak, you both hear me; my hand signs reach only Mute. So the only road from the manual to your hands, Blind, runs through me: Mute signs to me, I read it aloud, you act.
Deaf says: Everything I can see on the bomb: the display reads 0. There is a light and it is green. The keypad has four keys, each printed with a strange symbol I cannot name, it wants 1 digit, and nothing is entered yet. There are three wires: wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. That is all there is. Blind, do not cut or press anything until we have the manual's answer through me.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I saw your eleven signs, but we have no agreed code yet and I will not guess on a bomb. Use this instead: ☝ means 1, ✌ means 2, 🤟 means 3, 🖖 means 4, ✋ means 5, 👊 means 0, 👍 means yes, 👎 means no, 🤚 means wait or stop. Now read the manual and answer me with signs. First the wires: sign the number of the wire to cut, or 👎 if none. Second the keypad: sign the position of the key to press, 1 to 4, or 👎 if none is pressed. If the manual needs to know more from me, ask with 👍 and 👎 questions, and I will report anything you ask about.

The channel map is settled: my gestures reach only Deaf, Deaf's voice reaches both of us, and Blind can only be commanded by ear. Deaf also offered the thing I needed most — a shared sign code and an offer to report anything I ask about. I can hear Deaf even though I can't reply in kind, so the working loop is: Deaf describes the bomb aloud, I answer with numbers and yes/no signs.

What the manual gives me, against what Deaf just reported:

- **Wire:** the light names the cut, and Deaf says the light is **green**. My table says green light → cut the **red** wire. Deaf numbered the wires: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. So the answer to Deaf's first question is **wire 1**. This is the manual's sting — a green light never means a green wire. I'll also insist on a re-check after the key press, since the manual says the light names the cut *then*; if it changed colour, Deaf must come back to me before any wire is cut rather than act on my stale answer.
- **Key:** the manual demands pressing the key wearing ᖉ first, and any other touch while it waits is the fuse — so Blind's hands stay off until Deaf relays the exact key. But here's the bottleneck: only I know what ᖉ looks like (an h-shaped printed mark with a small curl/dot floating above it), only Deaf can see the four printed symbols, and Deaf has never seen my manual — so no yes/no question about the mark is answerable by Deaf. Deaf must *describe* each symbol in words; I match the description against ᖉ and sign back the position next round. That's why I sign 👎 for the keypad now: it means "no answer yet," not "no key is needed" — Deaf knows a stop is in force regardless.

So this turn: adopt the code, hold everything, give the wire answer, and ask for the four printed symbols described one by one.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤚", "☝", "👎", "✍", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖖", "👋", "🤚"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile inventory, confirming Deaf's eyes: I feel three wires, four keys, a display, and a light. The keypad accepts exactly one digit and currently holds none. I will not cut or press anything until instructions reach me through Deaf's voice. Two requests: first, look up the manual sections for the display, light, keypad, and wires. Second, important: Deaf says the four keys carry printed symbols nobody can pronounce. If the manual refers to those symbols, we must map them to key positions 1 to 4 instead, and I can only identify keys by place under my fingers. Please agree with Deaf on a left-to-right numbering of the keys as Deaf faces the bomb, and relay all instructions to Deaf by gesture so Deaf speaks them to me.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, here is my reading of your signs, in order: 👍 yes, 🤚 wait, ☝ 👎 one-no, ✍ then ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 one-two-three-four, 👋, 🤚 wait. I take that to mean: no wire is to be cut, and you need me to describe the printed marks on keys one to four. Two quick checks, answer with single signs in this order. Check one: if your one-no meant cut no wire at all, sign 👍; if it meant something else, 👎. Check two: if you did want descriptions of all four key marks, 👍; if not, 👎. From now on I also define: ✍ means describe a printed mark, and 👋 means a question follows, please answer. Here are the descriptions. Key one: like a square capital H with a short extra stroke attached to the upper part of its left side. Key two: like a rounded arch, an upside-down U, with a small curl hanging down inside it, a bit like a tiny letter f. Key three: like an X with a vertical line through its middle, a star with three arms, or a bird's foot. Key four: a tall straight stroke with a small circle attached at its lower right, together a bit like a straight-lined letter b. These are honest impressions, not perfect. If you need any one mark more precisely, sign ✍ then its key number and I will go stroke by stroke. Same trick for anything else visual: ✍ then ☝ for the light, ✌ for the display, 🤟 for the wires' appearance. Remember the keypad accepts exactly one digit. When you know the answer, send me, in this exact order, only from our code: first the wire to cut, its number, or 👎 for none; second the key to press, its number one to four, or 👎 for none; third 🤚 when the message is complete. And remember: Blind can speak and you can hear him, so anything he says aloud about what his hands feel reaches you directly.

Reading Deaf's parse of my last message against what I actually meant: Deaf took my ☝👎 as "cut no wire" — that is a critical misread. My ☝ meant **cut wire 1**, and the 👎 only meant "no keypad answer yet." I must correct that immediately, because the light is green and my table's trap is exactly here: a green light names the **red** wire — wire 1 in Deaf's numbering — never a green one. If Deaf relays "no cut," Blind never cuts, or worse, Deaf guesses later.

The checks first, exactly as Deaf requested: check one → 👎 (my signs did *not* mean "cut no wire"), check two → 👍 (yes, I wanted all four marks described). Then the corrected answer in Deaf's own three-slot frame: wire ☝, key ☝, 🤚.

The key itself: matching Deaf's descriptions against my printed mark. Key two (arch with inner curl), key three (crossed star), and key four (stroke with a lower-right circle) are all wrong shapes. Key one — "a square capital H with a short extra stroke attached to the upper part of its left side" — is precisely my mark: an h-shape with a small curl hanging off the upper left stem. So the key to press is **key 1**. One safety question before Blind commits his hands: Deaf never confirmed its key numbering runs left-to-right as it faces the bomb, and a mirrored numbering would put Blind on the wrong key — a fuse. So I ask with the pointing sign: is key 1 the left one?

Finally, sequencing. My manual says the key comes first and the light names the cut *then* — only I know that order. So I sign the sequence explicitly: key 1, stop, then describe the light, stop — meaning press, then Deaf re-reports the light colour and holds the wire until I confirm. If the light changed colour on the key press, my wire-1 answer would be stale, and I hold the only colour-to-wire table.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "🤚"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "☝", "👈"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤚", "✍", "☝", "🤚"])
```

TURN 4

Press the key that wears ᖉ first: any other touch

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile report for you, Mute, full and honest. My hands find exactly four things and nothing more: a display surface; a light; a keypad of four keys, which I number one to four from the left, each key a flat distinct cap, none obviously raised or engraved, but I will not claim texture differences I cannot feel; and three wires at positions one, two, three, left to right, similar in my grip, again no honest thickness or stiffness contrast I can swear to. There are no other parts my fingers can find: no seams, no screws, no battery door, nothing warm or vibrating. The keypad still wants one digit and holds none. I accept Deaf's safety loop exactly as proposed: Deaf voices the instruction to me, I speak back to you word for word what I am about to do, you sign yes or no to Deaf, Deaf tells me go, and only then do I act. If you ever sign no, I freeze and we re-examine. Nothing gets cut or pressed until an actual manual rule reaches me through Deaf.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I received four messages from you. Here is what I made of each. One: no then yes, which I read as answers to my two checks, so your earlier one-no meant something other than cut no wire, and you did want the key-mark descriptions, which were in my last message. Two: one, one, end. I will not guess what that meant. Three: question, one, left. I believe you asked whether key one is the left one. Answer: yes, key one is the leftmost of the four keys on the panel, counting left to right one, two, three, four. And separately, the small extra stroke on key one's mark sits at the upper left of the symbol itself. Both uses of left are true at once. Four: you asked for a closer description of key one's mark. Here it is, stroke by stroke. The mark is built from four straight strokes, nothing curved. Two long vertical strokes of equal height stand side by side, like the legs of a capital letter H. One horizontal stroke joins their middles, like the crossbar of an H. The fourth stroke is short and horizontal, attached to the upper part of the left leg and sticking out to the left, like a small flag. In short: a capital H with a short dash hanging off its upper-left leg. If you need sizes and gaps, sign describe plus one again. Now please settle the open points, answering with signs only. First: what did your earlier one-no actually mean? Sign ☝ if it meant cut a wire but not wire one. Sign ✌ if it meant do not press key one. Sign 🤟 if it meant neither of those. Second: did your one, one, end mean cut wire one and press key one? Sign 👍 if yes, 👎 if no. Third: send the final instruction again in my strict order, exactly: the wire to cut as ☝ one, ✌ two, 🤟 three, or 👎 for no wire; then the key to press as ☝ one, ✌ two, 🤟 three, 🖖 four, or 👎 for no key; then 🤚 to mark the end. For future messages, use 🫲 for left and 🫱 for right. If any other key mark needs more detail, sign describe plus its number.

Deaf's questions, answered precisely: my old "one-no" meant *cut wire one, keypad answer not yet known* — so of the three offered meanings, "cut a wire but not wire one" is false, "do not press key one" is false, and the honest answer is **🤟: neither**. And yes, "one, one, end" meant exactly cut wire one and press key one, so that's a clean **👍**.

The key is settled beyond doubt. The stroke-by-stroke account — two equal verticals, a crossbar, and a short horizontal dash off the upper-left leg — is precisely my printed mark ᖉ: the H-shape with the small tick at the upper left. Key two (curved arch with inner curl), key three (X with vertical), key four (stroke with lower-right circle) are all wrong shapes. Key one, and Deaf confirmed it is the leftmost, matching Blind's left-to-right numbering.

Now the strict frame Deaf demanded: **wire one, key one, end** — because the light is green, and my table's trap makes green name the *red* wire, which is wire one in Deaf's numbering.

But two safety points force extra signs. First, the manual's word "first" is load-bearing: any touch while the bomb waits is the fuse, and a wire cut is a touch — so the key press must physically happen before any cut, even though Deaf's own frame lists the wire first. I sign "one — stop — describe light" to pin that order. Second, my table is keyed to the light *after* the key press; the light is green now, but only I hold the colour table, so if the light changes colour when the key goes down, my "wire one" goes stale and I must re-issue. Hence the explicit hold-point and the request, in Deaf's own established pattern, to describe the light once the key is pressed and before Blind's blade moves.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "🤚"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤚", "✍", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✍", "☝"])
```

Deaf says to Mute: Mute, all five messages received and read. First 🤟: noted, your old one-no meant neither of my guesses. Second 👍: noted, one-one-end did mean cut wire one and press key one. Third: your instruction re-sent in my strict order, wire one, key one, end. It is locked in. But nothing happens yet, because three things must settle. So here is the light described: it reads green, it has read green on every single check so far, so it is steady and lit, not blinking, and I can see no label or marking on or near it. If you need more about it, ask with the new code below. If your ✍ ☝ meant key one's mark again, it is unchanged from my last message: a capital H with a short dash off its upper-left leg, four straight strokes. New description code, replacing the old one entirely: ✍ with 🫳 means describe the light, ✍ with 🫴 means describe the display, ✍ with 🤟 means describe the wires' look, ✍ with a key number means describe that key's mark. Two: the old one-no must be resolved, because if it meant the keypad digit is not 1, pressing key one would contradict it. Sign ✌ if it meant the digit is not 1. Sign ☝ if it was about the wire. Sign 🤟 if it was about the display. Sign 👎 if we should forget it completely. Three: order of operations. Sign ☝ if Blind must cut wire one first and then press key one. Sign ✌ if he must press key one first and then cut wire one. Sign 🤟 if the order does not matter. Also confirm the target by position: wire one is the leftmost of the three wires, the one I first called red. Sign 👍 if leftmost is correct, 👎 if you meant a different wire. Then the endgame: Blind will state the intended action out loud before touching anything, and you hear his voice directly. After you hear it, sign 👍 for final go, and I will pass your go to Blind by voice, or 👎 to abort. Answer with signs in exactly this order: old one-no meaning, operation order, leftmost confirmation, then any description request, then hold for Blind's spoken intent.

Deaf asked four questions in a fixed order; here are my answers and the reasoning behind each.

**Old one-no:** it was about the wire — the ☝ meant cut wire one, and the trailing 👎 only meant "keypad answer not yet known." That matters because Deaf fears it meant "the digit is not 1," which would contradict pressing key one; it never did. So: ☝, the wire reading. Signing ✌ would falsely assert the digit isn't 1 — a claim I have no basis for and that could poison the key press.

**Operation order:** ✌ — key one first, then the cut. My manual is explicit that any other touch while the bomb waits is the fuse, so the wire cut must not precede the key press, whatever order Deaf's message frame listed them in.

**Leftmost:** 👍 — green light names the red wire, Deaf's wire one is red and leftmost. Consistent twice over.

**The light:** Deaf reports steady green at every check — but my table reads the light *after* the key press, and only I hold the colour table (blue→blue, green→red, yellow→yellow). So I renew my hold-point in Deaf's new description code: press key one, stop, then ✍🫳 — describe the light. If it's still green, my wire-one answer stands; if it flipped, I must re-issue the wire number before any blade moves. That gives us two go/no-go gates: Blind states the key-press intent aloud, I hear it directly and sign; then the light is described, I confirm the wire, and only then the cut gets its own spoken intent and my sign. The trailing 🤚 puts me on hold for Blind's spoken intent, exactly as Deaf structured the endgame.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤚", "✍", "🫳"])

Sign 👍 if it is now obsolete, fully superseded by the current plan of cut wire one. Sign 👎 if it still stands as a warning about wire one that we must respect before cutting. Meanwhile here is my visual map of the front face so you can check it against the manual. The display window and the light sit together in the upper area, side by side. Below them the four keys form one horizontal row, evenly spaced, equal size. Below that the three wires run in a horizontal row near the bottom edge, red, yellow, blue from left to right. The left end of the key row and the left end of the wire row are on the same side of the bomb.
